description: Use case: the inheritance split of a securities depot into the parent portfolio and two child portfolios, respecting the lot sizes, as shown on the page 'Portfolio Split Calculator' (src/test/resources/web/html/use_cases/portfolio_split_calculator_sample.html). The inputs are the holdings, prices, lot sizes and exchange rates of the synthetic bank report (portfolio_report.json), the instruments and their issuers (portfolio_instruments.json) and the 30 / 35 / 35 split agreement with the agreed allocation of the two Lindt & Sprüngli holdings (portfolio_split_parameters_sample.json). The holdings are walked from the largest unit value times lot size to the smallest: the first child gets its target share of the holding value minus the deviation carried in from the holdings before, rounded to the lot size; the second child gets the same count, because both target shares are equal; the parent keeps the remainder, so every holding is conserved exactly; and the cash at the end, divisible to 0.01, closes the remaining drift to below one centime. The holding values, the remainder of the parent, the target values and the final split deviation are formulas of this file reproduced by the calc-validation; the rounding to the lot size and the carried deviation need a round function and a walk in a fixed order, so the allocations of the two children and the cumulative deviation after each step are stored as modelled values of the walk. The calculator triples of the base phrase portfolio split describe the page, so the system view Calculator shows the example portfolio split like the PV lifetime balance. ADDITIONALLY NEEDED, marked PROPOSED NEW ELEMENT in the keyword descriptions of calculator_keywords.json and described in docs/json_structure.md: (1) a repeated input 'calculator repeat' for the add and remove of children, whose result and walk columns follow the instances of child portfolio; (2) a checkbox field 'calculator checkbox' for mirror the children and split cash; (3) a read only field 'calculator read only' for the target weight of the parent; (4) a conditional text 'calculator warning' for the weight checks; (5) one collapsed section per detail table 'calculator section'; (6) number fields in a detail table 'calculator editable' for the holdings; (7) a column 'calculator phrase column' that shows the currency of the numbers of a holding; (8) the walk table parts 'calculator row number' and the order of the rows by the verb is ranked by to lot value; (9) the column colours 'calculator colour'; (10) the notes list 'calculator note'; (11) a check table 'calculator check' of the expected allocations of the split agreement; (12) a line diagram 'calculator diagram' of the cumulative deviation; (13) the buttons 'calculator file import', 'calculator download', 'calculator printable report' and 'calculator copy'; (14) 'calculator page independent' for the holdings, the walk, the exchange rates and the check, whose numbers do not have the page phrase; (15) the detail table rows over several levels of is a and is part of, e.g. LISP is a stock is a holding is part of split walk, and a cell that skips the numbers of another column, so that the count of a child is not taken for its cumulative deviation; (16) the lot value of each holding, which needs a formula per kind of holding before the walk can be ranked and the lot value column filled, and the target in units of the first child, which is only part of the descriptions of the modelled values so far; (17) the total of the realised portfolio value, which a value with realised value would let the split deviation formula calculate again for the whole depot; (18) in the engine a round to a multiple for the lot size, min and max for the clamp of the counts, a sum over a list for the weights of the children, a condition for the mirror and the split cash switch, a sort by a result and a walk that carries the deviation of one row into the next, because chars.php evaluates + - * / only; until then the walk results stay modelled values and an input change does not split again.

triples.name: portfolio split note rule
triples.description: A child's target is its weight times the position value, minus the deviation carried in from earlier positions. That target in units is rounded to the nearest round lot. With mirroring on, every child receives the first child's count. If the rounded counts together exceed the position, every child gets at most an equal part in round lots. The parent gets the rest, so every original position is conserved exactly.

triples.name: portfolio split note rule label
triples.description: Rule per position.

triples.name: portfolio split note deviation
triples.description: The carried deviation is the realised value minus the plain weighted value over all positions split so far, kept per child. It is subtracted once from the next target; it is not added again per step.

triples.name: portfolio split note deviation label
triples.description: Deviation.

triples.name: portfolio split note order
triples.description: LISP has a single unit of CHF 117,000. Rounding 3.5 shares to 4 gives the first child CHF 58,500 too much; the next positions take that back. With the sample data the stocks and bonds bring the drift down to about CHF 13 per child; splitting the cash then closes the gap to below one centime.
